Meaning: To give money that must be given back.
Example: The bank is lending you that money.
Note: lend = I give. borrow = I take. Most common mix-up.

Meaning: To take money that you must give back.
Example: When you are young you spend more than you earn, so you borrow.

Meaning: To pay money back.
Example: Companies repay it from future profits.

Meaning: To officially create and offer something, like bonds or shares.
Example: Governments borrow by issuing bonds.

Meaning: To collect money for a purpose.
Example: Companies raise money now to invest and grow.

Meaning: To provide money for something.
Example: Governments borrow to fund schools and roads.

Meaning: To decide where something should go and send it there.
Example: Price is the signal that allocates resources.

Meaning: To make something easier or possible.
Example: There is a system that facilitates all of this.

Meaning: To get money by working, or to get a return on money.
Example: Mid-life: you earn a bit more than you spend.

Meaning: To ask for something firmly, as a condition.
Example: Investors demand more return when risk is higher.

Meaning: To cancel out, by having something equal on the other side.
Example: A loss on one side is cancelled by a gain on the other.

Meaning: To fix a price or rate now, so it cannot change later.
Example: An airline can lock in its jet-fuel cost.

Meaning: To follow and copy the movement of something.
Example: A derivative is priced off the asset it tracks.

Meaning: To go up, by itself.
Example: When rates rise, bond prices fall.
Note: rise = it goes up. raise = I lift something. Prices rise; the bank raises rates.

Meaning: To go down.
Example: Price falls from GBP 100 to GBP 91.58.

Meaning: Not changing much; at the same level.
Example: Income goes up and down, but you want steady spending.

Meaning: To go up and down repeatedly, in an unstable way.
Example: Crypto fluctuates a lot.

Meaning: To make smaller.
Example: Add up every future cash flow, but shrink each one.

Meaning: A situation where more of one thing means less of another.
Example: Higher return comes with more risk. That trade-off is Pillar 2.

Meaning: The general direction something moves over time.
Example: I think this is a temporary trend.

Meaning: By a large amount; in a way that matters.
Example: The same need, but scaled up very significantly.

Meaning: To accept something as true without proving it, so you can continue.
Example: Perfect competition assumes perfect information.
Note: You will need this in every economics essay.

Meaning: Facts or data that show something is true.
Example: Base it on real data and cite a reputable source.

Meaning: To name the source you took information from.
Example: Cite a reputable source.

Meaning: Trusted and respected.
Example: Make sure it is a reputable source, not social media.

Meaning: The ability to decide well when the answer is not obvious.
Example: More value on judgment, client trust, and asking the right questions.

Meaning: Examining something carefully instead of accepting it.
Example: "Critical means a lot of iterations. Why this? Why that?"

Term: in the long run / in the short run
Meaning: Over a long period / over a short period.
Example: In the long run, equities returned 5.3% a year.

Meaning: No matter what; without it making a difference.
Example: Irrespective of what career you are thinking of pursuing.

Meaning: To include something when you think or calculate.
Example: You have got to take the fact that AI is evolving into account.

Meaning: To try to achieve or follow a career or project.
Example: A strong footing to pursue a finance career.

Meaning: To do less than you should, and end up late.
Example: If you are falling behind and have not done anything for two weeks.

Meaning: The basic ideas everything else is built on.
Example: "These foundations will not change in the next 30 years."

Meaning: To have as your property.
Example: The left side of a balance sheet is what the firm OWNS.
Note: own (asset) vs owe (liability). One letter apart, opposite meaning.

Meaning: To have to pay someone.
Example: Liabilities are what it OWES.

Meaning: To be equal on both sides.
Example: The two sides must always balance.

Meaning: To make bigger or stronger.
Example: Leverage magnifies returns AND losses.

Meaning: To take in and soak up.
Example: Capital absorbs the loss first.

Meaning: A hard choice between two options, both with drawbacks.
Example: The right-hand side is a dilemma: debt or equity.

Meaning: To receive something you did not choose.
Example: You largely inherit your business risk.
Note: Paired with "to choose" on the slide.

Meaning: On purpose, by choice.
Example: You deliberately choose your financial risk.

Meaning: Something in the real world that stops the perfect version from holding.
Example: The real world adds two frictions: the tax shield and distress cost.

Meaning: Able to be taken off your income before tax is calculated.
Example: Interest is tax-deductible, so debt lowers the tax bill.

Meaning: Serious trouble, close to failing.
Example: Those who cannot roll it over affordably tip into distress.

Meaning: To fail completely and suddenly.
Example: Carillion collapsed owing billions.

Meaning: To have a position in an order of priority.
Example: Mezzanine debt ranks behind senior lenders.

Meaning: Something you are required to do.
Example: Equity has no obligation to pay anything.

Meaning: Not required; you may choose.
Example: Dividends are optional.

Meaning: The potential gain if things go well.
Example: Equity owns all the growth and all the upside.

Meaning: Limited to a maximum.
Example: Debt's return is capped at its interest.

Meaning: Something that mixes two different types.
Example: A preference share is a debt-equity hybrid.

Meaning: The other side in a deal.
Example: A principal stands in the middle as counterparty.

Meaning: To carry and suffer.
Example: Each transformer bears the risk.

Meaning: The gap between two prices or rates, kept as profit.
Example: It earns the spread rather than a simple fee.

Meaning: A buffer that protects you from a blow.
Example: A wafer-thin ~5% cushion.

Meaning: Extremely thin.
Example: Lloyds has a wafer-thin cushion.

Meaning: To change something into something quite different.
Example: A bank transforms short safe deposits into long risky loans.

Meaning: To take money out.
Example: It must always find cash for today's withdrawals.

Meaning: Easily broken.
Example: A bank is fragile.

Meaning: To run away, fast.
Example: Deposits now flee faster than the rulebook assumed.

Meaning: To set off suddenly.
Example: The run was sparked on group chats and X.

Meaning: To tell the difference.
Example: "A classic problem is to distinguish illiquidity from insolvency."

Meaning: Healthy and reliable; not damaged.
Example: Its loans are sound.
Note: NOT "a sound you hear". Here it means healthy.

Meaning: Completely out of money; finished.
Example: Genuinely bust: it owes more than it owns.
Note: Informal but used in the slides.

Meaning: To bring under control.
Example: Together they tame the fragility.

Meaning: To knock over.
Example: A bank today is harder to topple than in 2007.

Meaning: The final support behind everything else.
Example: The central bank is the final backstop.

Meaning: To guide the direction of something.
Example: The cost of borrowing is how the central bank steers the money supply.

Meaning: To make something run smoothly.
Example: Banks provide the credit that lubricates the economy.

Meaning: When your duties to two sides clash.
Example: Whose side is it on?

Meaning: To escape where it should not go.
Example: Information that must not leak.

Meaning: Something that blocks passage.
Example: Chinese walls are strict information barriers.

Meaning: To keep apart.
Example: The US legally separates commercial and investment banking.

Meaning: To cancel a law.
Example: Gramm-Leach-Bliley tears the wall down.

Meaning: The moment the consequences arrive.
Example: 2008: the reckoning.

Meaning: To exchange one thing for another.
Example: Each note was swappable for a fixed amount of gold.

Meaning: To support it with something of value.
Example: It is not backed by gold.

Meaning: To keep its value over time.
Example: A store of value holds its worth.

Meaning: To lose slowly.
Example: Money is designed to leak slowly.

Meaning: To run after.
Example: More money chasing the same goods.

Meaning: To get rid of fast, without caring about the price.
Example: Everyone dumps the currency.

Meaning: Not physical; existing only as an idea.
Example: Money keeps getting more abstract.

Meaning: To cut sharply.
Example: To sell a house fast you must slash the price.

Meaning: Not available, because it is locked into something.
Example: Rich but illiquid: all your money tied up in property.

Meaning: To disappear completely.
Example: The moment everyone reaches for cash, liquidity evaporates.

Meaning: To get bigger (of a gap).
Example: The gap between buying and selling widened tenfold.

Meaning: By ten times.
Example: It widened tenfold.

Meaning: To reach the day it must be paid.
Example: Bills come due in cash, not in assets.

Meaning: To stop letting people take their money out.
Example: UK property funds had to shut their doors to withdrawals.

Meaning: Easily harmed; needing protection.
Example: Cash still matters for the vulnerable.

Meaning: The hidden machinery that makes a system work.
Example: The plumbing behind a cashless payment.

Meaning: To check that something is true.
Example: Thousands of computers race to verify the payment.

Meaning: To change the record of what happened.
Example: Each block is locked to the one before, so nobody can rewrite history.

Meaning: The hidden drawback.
Example: The catch: no deposit insurance.

Meaning: Serious danger.
Example: The peril: privacy and the banks.

Meaning: To put the pieces together.
Example: Four lectures built the pieces. Today we assemble them.

Meaning: To direct along a particular path.
Example: Banks and markets channel the money.

Meaning: A rule that has no exceptions.
Example: One sector's deficit must be another's surplus. Always.

Meaning: There is no other possibility.
Example: The iron rule we will prove today.

Meaning: To be the one who suffers the loss.
Example: Households bear ALL the risk.

Meaning: Finally, after everything else.
Example: Every loss lands on people in the end.

Meaning: To rise very fast and very high.
Example: Greek interest rates soared.

Meaning: To rise suddenly.
Example: 30-year yields jumped from under 4% to about 5% in three days.

Meaning: Continuing for a long time, not going away.
Example: China and Germany run persistent surpluses.

Meaning: To have one, over a period of time.
Example: The government runs a deficit.
Note: Fixed collocation. Learn it as a whole.

Term: to sum to zero / to add up to zero
Meaning: To cancel out exactly when added together.
Example: The balances always sum to zero.

Meaning: Fixed, with no freedom to change.
Example: Know three balances and the fourth is locked.

Meaning: To create space for something else.
Example: Cut one sector's deficit and another balance must move to make room.

Meaning: To break suddenly.
Example: When confidence snaps, the flows reverse.

Meaning: To turn the other way.
Example: A sector cut off overnight: the flows reverse.

Meaning: Very suddenly, in no time at all.
Example: A sector can be cut off overnight.

Meaning: Harsh and without mercy.
Example: Reversals are fast and brutal.

Meaning: To avoid by moving quickly.
Example: Chasing returns and dodging sudden stops.

Meaning: To hold something firmly in place.
Example: The risk-free rate anchors all of finance.

Meaning: In its most basic nature.
Example: Every one of these jobs is, at heart, reading the four sectors.

Meaning: Far too much of something.
Example: The global savings glut.

Meaning: To make something swell up beyond its real value.
Example: It helped inflate the 2008 housing bubble.
